newsitem.title: USA: Texaco defends combination plan with Shell.
newsitem.headline: Texaco defends combination plan with Shell.

text.p: Texaco Inc on Friday defended the proposal to merge its refining and marketing operations in the western half of the United States with Shell Oil Co.

Five consumer groups Friday urged the Federal Trade Commission to block the merger, saying it would stifle competition in the West Coast market, which has already seen the loss of several independent refiners and marketers.
But Texaco said the merger had to go through, otherwise the company would join the list of casualties in a world of tight refining margins and high capital costs.
"We have a compelling case why we have to do this," Texaco spokesman Jim Swords told Reuters. "What will ultimately happen is we will disappear, if we continue in the environment we're in."

He said by combining transportation operations, the merged company will be in a stronger position to supply the wide array of fuels required by the market, "better than each company can do separately right now."
That would allow the companies to "ultimately offer competitively priced products," he said.
